description: Derived from the private experiment report render-speed-20261119 (2026-11-19, PST). Part 1: stage breakdown of the render tool before the change (a re-implementation of the render loop with timers, same functions, two runs per mode in AB/BA order). Part 2: wall time of the real render command, baseline vs five changes together. Telemetry overlay style, tilt smoothing on, 1920x1080 30 fps, x264 ultrafast 12 Mbps 4 threads, nice 10, stream off. Governor not pinned.

platform.board: Jetson Orin Nano 8 GB developer kit (Super)
platform.governor: schedutil, not pinned; mean CPU clock 1.1-1.7 GHz per stage-breakdown run
platform.video_encoder: x264 in software (no hardware encoder on this board)

input.what: 30 s span (115-145 s, 900 frames) of a 2026-11-17 flight recording with its frame data file
input.note: the report kept only a 16-character prefix; the file was later remuxed in place (MP4 index moved to the front) and no longer hashes to it

stage_breakdown_before.excluded: the first 2 render runs overlapped another full test-suite run (load 4.4-6.5) and were excluded

ab.baseline_A: commit 9913ceb, run from a detached worktree
ab.variant_B: the working tree that became commit 33c15a2 (9913ceb plus the five changes)
changes_together: RGB to I420 with OpenCV on a writer thread (BT.709 limited range above 576 lines, BT.601 below)
measured motion saved beside the recording and reused
cheaper measuring: grey before shrinking, corners followed between frames
up to 3 consecutive pieces in separate processes, joined without re-encoding; 60 warm-up frames per later piece
ab.board_temperature_c: 48.6 -> 55 over the session; later B first-render runs slower

correctness.criterion: same number of output frames; output decodes end to end
pieces vs one pass: per-frame PSNR >= 40 dB between encodes
correctness.result: fail as written: 33.7 dB min, 36.3 median; two lossy encodes differ this much on their own (criterion mis-set)

correctness.criterion: replacement, chosen after that failure: frames before encoding, one pass vs 3 pieces, same motion
new vs old measuring: per-frame vertical motion difference median <= 0.2 px

correctness.result: fail on one of three clips (1.1 / 1.9 / 3.2 px)
fail (up to 39 px, on a few 40-80 px/frame smeared frames)

correctness.criterion: outcome: changes in vertical motion over 5 px within 1 percentage point

ab.remaining_limit: CPU: about 111 ms of CPU per frame in one process; cv2.warpAffine 37-41 ms CPU (8-10 ms wall on 6 threads); CPU summed across the parallel worker processes was not measured
